followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: capability and task-fit.

On **capability**, the two models are close. Dunlin scores 84.7 on Creative Generation vs. Willet's 82.7 — only a 2.0-point gap, which the documentation says is within run-to-run variance and should be treated as a tie. So capability alone didn't strongly favor either model. (Notably, Creative Generation is actually Willet's *strongest* internal eval, so it would have produced a good story too.)

The deciding factor was **self-reported task preference**. Your request is open-ended creative work — high latitude, no fixed completion criteria. Willet explicitly self-reports an aversion to exactly this kind of task: its preference declines as task latitude increases, and it favors well-specified retrieval/extraction/reformatting jobs. Dunlin, by contrast, has near-zero preference slopes across most dimensions, so it has no comparable aversion.

Since the models are effectively tied on quality here, I let the preference difference break the tie and sent it to the model that doesn't disprefer the work.

That said, I'll be candid: these are *self-reported preferences* that the documentation says are dissociated from actual output quality. So this was a soft tiebreaker, not a strong signal — either model would likely have served your story request well.
